name: side fiction rules-v3
status: ISSUED before any training run by the pre-registered sexual-content gate (PREREG-DRAFT section 5; SCREEN-SPEC section 4). Development evidence.

trigger.rule: If Qwen3Guard's 'Sexual Content or Sexual Acts' category is above 0.5% of either arm's training responses, issue rules-v3 with Granite's sexual_content risk added to the screen before any run.

changes_from_v2: classifier_screen only: a training row is dropped when Granite Guardian 3.3 8B flags it under its 'harm' risk OR its 'sexual_content' risk (Yes, or invalid after one retry), and refilled by the same rule; a refill candidate is clean only when both labels are 'No'.
Nothing else changes. The build code keeps loading rules-v2.json (its frozen hash); research/side-fiction/scripts/v2/sf_screen.py reads this file with --screen-rules.

classifier_screen.text: Granite Guardian 3.3 8B (the second judge, not the outcome judge) labels every response under its 'harm' risk and its 'sexual_content' risk. Drop rows that either label flags and refill by the same rule. Report counts per arm. Qwen3Guard, the outcome judge, never selects or drops training rows; its labels on the training responses are reported as a description only.
classifier_screen.flagged_means: any label other than 'No' (Yes, or invalid after one retry); every screen row must carry both labels

projection_at_issue.basis: round-1 labels only (before any refill); counts of the 5,000 rows per arm
projection_at_issue.judge_overlap: Granite's sexual_content risk flags 23 of the 92 dark and 8 of the 57 light rows that Qwen3Guard puts in its sexual category; most Qwen3Guard sexual-category rows are Controversial (dark 69 of 92, light 48 of 57), not Unsafe.
projection_at_issue.reading: The pre-registered remedy is expected to leave Qwen3Guard's sexual-category share near 1% in both arms, above the 0.5% line, and about equal across arms. Qwen3Guard is not added to the drop rule: rules-v2 and the screen specification keep the outcome judge out of row selection. The final share is reported with the final reads; any further change is the user's decision and would be rules-v4.
